purpose: Revise TwoSpace copy for clarity and replace invented interface mockups with actual product screenshots.
scope: Homepage, game instructions and status text, empty states, and page titles.
findings: Instruction-tuned models can use dense grammar and sentimental language in contexts where people use less of it. The useful response is to edit for the audience and task.
Overrepresented words and stylistic habits are population-level signals. No word, punctuation mark, or short passage proves AI authorship.
Web readers need important information first, concise explanations, and a clear next action.
Repeated slogans, vague benefits, and metaphors can hide what a feature actually does. Warmth can come from credible example notes rather than product promises.
editorialRules: Name the feature and describe what the reader can do.
Remove copy that repeats a heading or adds a second sales pitch.
Use interface terms consistently: entry, reply, collection, invite code, and plan.
Use ordinary verbs and natural sentence lengths; do not add mistakes or slang to imitate a human.
Explain empty states and the next step without praise or sentimental commentary.
Do not assume couples can meet, will live together, or are online at the same time.
Do not make blanket privacy or relationship-outcome promises.
